reason: Fast Landing evaluator-repair successor after the route prerequisite merged on trusted main. The remaining defect is that delegated governance currently allows the immutable first failure-first implementation head to be created from an effective authorization merge even when trusted main has already advanced. This authorization limits the repair to the owning trusted evaluator plus its existing policy test and requires an opt-in first-head trusted-main guard so drift fails closed before that first head can be accepted as causal RED evidence.

requiredSemantics: Only delegated authorizations that explicitly declare the exact first-head trusted-main guard are subject to the new behavior.
On the unique first failure-first implementation head, trusted main must equal the effective authorization merge commit.
If trusted main advanced before that first head is evaluated, the branch fails closed with WP0_DELEGATED_GOVERNANCE_FIRST_HEAD_MAIN_DRIFT before the head can count as causal RED evidence.
After a valid first failure-first head, existing delegated governance fresh-main refresh semantics remain unchanged.
Existing authorizations without the declaration preserve current behavior.
The guard must derive authority from the trusted authorization merged on main; candidate-owned text cannot weaken or bypass it.
forbiddenWeakening: Do not weaken authorization merge topology checks.
Do not permit candidate-owned main snapshots or PR prose to substitute for trusted main.
Do not broaden governance routing or mutate wp0-routing-policy.json.
Do not alter dependency, workflow, Product, Model Brain, local auxiliary runtime or Desktop/Windows UAT surfaces.
